q: Isolated chlorophyll molecules in solution glow red (fluoresce) when illuminated, instead of passing electrons on. What does this reveal about photosystems?
options: Isolated chlorophyll is destroyed by light, so it can no longer absorb any photons
Chlorophyll in solution absorbs only red light, so it simply reflects all of that red light back out
Without the array and a nearby acceptor, excited electrons just drop back, re-emitting the energy
Isolated chlorophyll makes O2 instead of transferring electrons, which causes the glow
explanation: An excited electron in an isolated pigment returns to its ground state within nanoseconds, releasing energy as light (fluorescence) and heat. In a photosystem, proteins hold the pigments in a precise array so energy is funnelled to the reaction centre, which sits beside a primary electron acceptor that captures the electron before it can drop back. A single pigment molecule can't do any of this.
